name: license_status
description: Show whether this server runs in free or Pro mode and where to upgrade.

name: license_activate
description: Activate a Pro license key (format MCPL1.xxx.yyy). Verified offline and saved locally.

arguments.name: key
arguments.desc: License key from the checkout confirmation page

name: sheet_info
description: Open an xlsx or csv file and describe it: sheet names, size, guessed header row, per-column type, sample values and empty counts. Start here before reading or querying.

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Path to the .xlsx/.xlsm/.xlsb/.ods/.csv/.tsv file (~ is expanded)

name: sheet_read
description: Read rows from a sheet as a text table, JSON records or CSV. Use limit/offset to page through big files, or range for an A1 block like B2:F40.

arguments.name: sheet
arguments.desc: Sheet name; defaults to the first sheet

arguments.name: range
arguments.desc: A1 range such as A1:D50; overrides limit/offset

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Rows to return, default 100

arguments.name: offset
arguments.desc: Rows to skip, default 0

arguments.name: as
arguments.desc: Output format, default table

name: sheet_query
description: Filter, pick columns and sort rows without writing any code. where uses a small safe expression language: comparisons = != > >= < <= plus contains / startswith / endswith, combined with AND, OR, NOT and parentheses. Column names with spaces go in brackets: [Unit Price] > 10 AND [Region] contains "north". Strings use single or double quotes.

arguments.name: where
arguments.desc: Filter, e.g. [Qty] >= 5 AND ([Status] = "open" OR [Status] = "new")

arguments.name: select
arguments.desc: Column names to return; default all

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Default 100

name: sheet_stats
description: Per-column count, empty count, distinct values, min, max, sum, mean and median. Numbers are parsed from currency and percent text too.

arguments.name: columns
arguments.desc: Limit to these columns; default all

name: sheet_find
description: Search every cell for text (case insensitive) and return cell addresses with a preview of the row it is on.

arguments.name: text
arguments.desc: Text to look for

arguments.name: sheet
arguments.desc: Sheet name; default searches every sheet

name: sheet_write
description: Write rows to a spreadsheet. rows may be objects (keys become headers) or arrays (first array is the header row). mode new_file writes a brand new file and refuses to clobber an existing one; append adds the rows under the existing data; overwrite replaces the file contents. Format follows the extension of out_path (.xlsx, .csv, .tsv, .json).

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Source file for append/overwrite, or the intended file for new_file

arguments.name: rows
arguments.desc: Array of objects, or array of arrays with a header row first

arguments.name: out_path
arguments.desc: Where to write; default is a new file next to the source for new_file, or the source itself for append/overwrite

name: sheet_add_column
description: Add a computed column and save the result to a NEW file (the source is never modified unless out_path points at it). formula uses the same expression language as sheet_query over the columns of each row, e.g. "[Qty] * [Unit Price]" or '[Country] = "PL"'. Alternatively pass values, one per data row.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Name of the new column

arguments.name: formula
arguments.desc: Expression over row columns, e.g. "[Qty] * [Unit Price]"

arguments.name: values
arguments.desc: Explicit values, one per data row

arguments.name: out_path
arguments.desc: Output file; default <source>-plus-<column>.<same ext>

name: sheet_convert
description: Convert a sheet to csv, xlsx or json. Writes a new file next to the source unless out_path is given.
